prs.cluster_pick_reason: 3056's helper strips Annotated wrappers before inspecting union members (_unwrap_annotated), so it correctly skips pre-parsing for the common real-world case `Annotated[str, Field(...)] | None` -- a case 2032's _should_pre_parse_json misses, since it compares raw args against a fixed simple-type set without unwrapping Annotated, causing Annotated[str,...] to be treated as a non-simple type and still trigger the bug. 3056 also scopes the skip strictly to str-only unions (str | None) rather than 2032's broader 'all args are simple types' rule, which would also silently disable pre-parsing for str|int and str|bool unions -- a behavior change beyond the reported bug that 2032's diff does not add test coverage for.

prs.author: arimu1
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Concurrent/duplicate JSON-RPC request ids sharing the same key in `_request_streams` cause response cross-wiring (one request receives another's payload, or one hangs) because the routing key was not guaranteed unique per in-flight request. (2 PRs)

prs.cluster_pick_reason: Both PRs add rejection of an in-flight duplicate request id, but #3221 fixes two additional edge cases that #3063 leaves open: (1) #3063 keys streams with `str(message.id)`, which collapses distinct JSON-RPC ids `1` (int) and `"1"` (string) into the same key, so a string id can still false-positive a 409 against, or cross-wire with, a numeric id already in flight; (2) that same `str()` coercion means a client-supplied string id equal to `_GET_stream` (GET_STREAM_KEY) could collide with the standalone GET stream slot. #3221 introduces a type-preserving `_request_stream_key()` (prefixing `i:`/`s:` by type) that closes both gaps while implementing the same duplicate-id rejection behavior as #3063.

clusters.pick_reason: Both PRs add rejection of an in-flight duplicate request id, but #3221 fixes two additional edge cases that #3063 leaves open: (1) #3063 keys streams with `str(message.id)`, which collapses distinct JSON-RPC ids `1` (int) and `"1"` (string) into the same key, so a string id can still false-positive a 409 against, or cross-wire with, a numeric id already in flight; (2) that same `str()` coercion means a client-supplied string id equal to `_GET_stream` (GET_STREAM_KEY) could collide with the standalone GET stream slot. #3221 introduces a type-preserving `_request_stream_key()` (prefixing `i:`/`s:` by type) that closes both gaps while implementing the same duplicate-id rejection behavior as #3063.

members.cluster_pick_reason: All three add a custom __reduce__ to fix the same pickle TypeError, but at different scopes. #2555 patches only UrlElicitationRequiredError.__reduce__, so any other MCPError subclass with a non-matching constructor is still broken after this PR. #2478 adds a base-level _restore_mcp_error helper but hardcodes a special-case branch for UrlElicitationRequiredError (calling from_error/from_error_data), which reconstructs the instance from ErrorData rather than from its actual __dict__, risking loss of subclass-specific state not encoded in ErrorData. #3262 instead defines __reduce__ once on the MCPError base class using MCPError.__new__(error_type) + Exception.__init__(restored, *args) plus the instance __dict__ as reduce state, so it round-trips any subclass generically with no per-subclass special-casing, and its test diff explicitly exercises a second subclass (NoBackChannelError) to prove the fix isn't limited to UrlElicitationRequiredError.

clusters.pick_reason: Both PRs add rejection of an in-flight duplicate request id, but #3221 fixes two additional edge cases that #3063 leaves open: (1) #3063 keys streams with `str(message.id)`, which collapses distinct JSON-RPC ids `1` (int) and `"1"` (string) into the same key, so a string id can still false-positive a 409 against, or cross-wire with, a numeric id already in flight; (2) that same `str()` coercion means a client-supplied string id equal to `_GET_stream` (GET_STREAM_KEY) could collide with the standalone GET stream slot. #3221 introduces a type-preserving `_request_stream_key()` (prefixing `i:`/`s:` by type) that closes both gaps while implementing the same duplicate-id rejection behavior as #3063.
